title: Real Estate Brokerage Automation Software: 2026 Guide
summary: Real estate brokerage automation software automates lead follow-up, paperwork, and app handoffs.
body_markdown:
## Zapier app automation


Where SkySlope leaves the handoffs between apps open, Zapier does that work. It connects apps you already run through triggers and actions, with no code, so a new row in one tool starts a step in another.


It earns a place in a brokerage only for those gaps between specialists.


Think of a Zap as one trigger followed by one or more actions. Typical brokerage uses are a form submission creating a contact in your CRM and a signed document posting a note to a team channel.


Check the trigger before you commit. A catalogue of thousands of apps says little; what matters is whether your CRM exposes the specific trigger you need, such as "new lead" or "stage changed", and the fields you need to map.


Look up your own CRM and transaction tools in Zapier's app directory first, because real estate coverage varies app by app.


If the trigger you need isn't in a closed directory, you wait on the vendor's roadmap rather than your own. Activepieces lets you generate the missing integration with AI and add it privately to your own instance, with no vendor release in the way.


Its 750 integrations are counted straight from the` packages/pieces/community` folder of the open-source monorepo on GitHub, roughly 60% of them contributed by the community, and the core carries the MIT licence in the repository's LICENSE file (the` packages/ee/` directories sit under a separate commercial licence), so you're reliant on community maintenance for most of your integrations.


MoneyGram and Moneypenny run it in production.


Because Zapier bills by task, meaning each action step that runs, a five-step Zap uses several tasks per lead.


The table shows the three tiers and how quickly the allowance shrinks against real lead volume, by the time most teams are running real volume, they've already stepped up to a higher tier.


Plan Monthly price Tasks


Free $0 100


Professional $19.99 750


Team $103.50 2,000


To get shared use with 25 users, you need Team, turning collaboration into a premium-tier feature, which means smaller teams are locked out of this functionality.


The free plan suits a trial of one workflow, since a brokerage with steady inbound leads would exhaust 100 tasks quickly.


Because each added step multiplies usage, cost climbs with volume rather than with team size.


If your data must stay on your own servers, Zapier isn't an option, because it is a hosted service.


It suits a broker or office manager who needs a handful of connections between tools they already pay for, and who wants to maintain them without a developer.


Skip it as your main system for lead follow-up or transaction compliance, where a specialist covers the whole job. Skip it too if high volume with many steps per record would make task billing your largest line item.
